criteria.criterion: A test in crates/athena-core shows that a request naming an existing file with a boundary word (such as BRIEF.md or a docs file) but whose own text has none is admitted. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: The new test commits BRIEF.md and docs/dirty.md, each holding a banned word built by concat. It asserts scan_request_input finds nothing, that `queue` (ask --later) admits the request and moves head, and that `ask` returns a reading and moves head again. It passed when I ran it (1 passed). With the old file loop, both calls would have returned the 'not admitted' error.

criteria.criterion: A test shows that a request whose own text holds a boundary word is still refused with a 'not admitted' error naming source `request`. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: The new test sends a request that names a clean BRIEF.md and holds a banned word on line 2. It asserts that both `ask` and `queue` fail with 'not admitted' and 'request:2: <word>', that head is unchanged, and that scan_request_input returns exactly one InputFinding{source:"request",line:2}. It passed when I ran it.

criteria.criterion: `scan_request_input` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs no longer reads named files at admission, and its doc comment and the `refuse_banned_input` message describe request-only scanning. The old test in run/mod.rs that expected a named dirty file to be refused is replaced.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: scan_request_input is now `fn(text: &str) -> Vec<InputFinding>`. It has no git or treeish parameters and no request_text_touches loop. Its doc comment says it scans 'the request's own text only'. The refuse_banned_input doc comment and bail message now say 'its own text holds words...', and 'or a file it names' is gone. Grep finds no remaining reference to the old test name `a_named_file_with_a_banned_word_is_flagged_with_path_and_line_and_a_clean_one_is_not`, and the two new tests replace it.

criteria.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` pass.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks on this tree: fmt passed, clippy -D warnings passed, and cargo test --locked passed with 1646 tests.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry saying admission scans only the request's own text, not the files it names, and says why: the owner's brief legitimately uses boundary words.
criteria.evidence: A new bullet under Unreleased > Changed says admission (`athena ask`, including `--later`) scans only the request's own text, not the files it names. It gives the reason (the owner's brief legitimately uses boundary words), cites the 2026-10-29 refusal, and notes that files are still scanned when a candidate changes them. It does not spell out any banned word.

criteria.criterion: The change refuses fewer readings, not more; no new refusal rule is added. Expected 0% of newly refused readings.
criteria.evidence: The diff only removes the named-file loop. No bail! or refusal condition is added, and boundary_scan and the word lists are untouched. Athena's replay shows 0 of 50 accepted readings are newly refused. The request-text refusal still works (test passed).

findings.summary: Two changed files are outside the expected deliverables: docs/enforcement.md and xtask/tests/policy.rs.
findings.evidence: The docs/enforcement.md edit is required: policy test M24 (xtask/tests/policy.rs:508-515) fails if a test named in the map no longer exists, and the old test was deleted. The policy.rs edit changes only a comment so it describes the new behavior. Both are small and justified, but neither is on the deliverables list.

findings.summary: admission.rs is on the deliverables list but was not changed.

summary: The change passes. It fixes the root cause in `scan_request_input`, which now scans only the request's own text and no longer reads the files a request names. Both entry points (`ask` and `ask --later`) use it. I ran the two new tests in athena-core and both pass: a request that names a BRIEF.md and a docs file holding a banned word is admitted, and a request whose own text holds a banned word is still refused with 'not admitted' and 'request:2: <word>', with nothing recorded. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs all passed, and the CHANGELOG entry gives the change and its reason. No new refusal rule is added, and Athena's replay found 0 of 50 accepted readings newly refused. One minor scope finding: docs/enforcement.md and a comment in xtask/tests/policy.rs changed outside the deliverables list. The docs edit is needed because the policy test M24 fails when the enforcement map names a test that no longer exists.
